newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan high-tech shares revive on hopes of recovery.
newsitem.headline: Japan high-tech shares revive on hopes of recovery.

text.p: Shares in the high-technology sector rose in Wednesday morning trade in Tokyo, buoyed by hopes that the semiconductor industry is on the road to recovery, brokers said.

Brokers said buying interest was focusing on high-tech shares due to bullishness in the U.S. NASDAQ composite index, which has recovered to the 1,200 level. Many high-technology shares are listed on NASDAQ.
They added that signs of recovery in spot prices for 16 megabit DRAM chips, the most popular type, were also encouraging investors.
Brokerage Morgan Stanley told Reuters earlier that spot prices have risen to $10 from $8 in early August.
At 0041 GMT, NEC Corp shares were 40 yen higher at 1,270. Its trade volume was the largest on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange at 5.787 million shares.
Fujitsu Ltd, which had the third-largest trade volume at 4.233 million shares, was 21 yen higher at 1,020 yen.
Toshiba Corp shares were up 23 yen at 728 yen on a trade volume of 2.278 million shares.
Advantest, a manufacturer of semiconductor testing devices, was up 80 yen at 4,170 yen on volume of 1.734 million.
Wednesday is first day of trade for October delivery and also the start of trade for the latter half of the fiscal year, and market sources said this reduced pressure to buy in a hurry.

"Institutional investors and public funds are starting to buy major issues which they have been hesitating to buy over these past couple of months and they are starting with semiconductor shares, which are looking a bit optimistic," said Haruo Nakaharu, a strategist at Toyo Securities.
